column1: # credentials.tsv - the credentials this repository knows how to rotate.
# Tab-separated. Blank lines and lines beginning with # are ignored.
# credential-rotation.sh is the only thing that reads it.
# COLUMNS
#   id            stable handle, used as --id. Never renamed once written down.
#   parameter     the SSM Parameter Store path. This is a pointer, not a value.
#   rotate_days   how long a value may live before `due` calls it overdue.
#   coexist       yes - old and new are both valid for a while, so the rotation
#                       has an overlap window and can be verified before the old
#                       value is revoked
#                 no  - the moment the new value exists the old one is dead, so
#                       the sync has to be immediate and there is no way back
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A COLUMN
#   Which ExternalSecrets consume a parameter. That is discovered from the
#   cluster at run time rather than copied here, for two reasons. A copied list
#   goes stale the first time somebody adds a consumer and nobody remembers to
#   edit this file, and the whole point of `rotate` is that it reaches every
#   consumer - a fan-out taken from a stale copy would miss one silently. It
#   also keeps this file free of cluster object names, which matters because
#   this repository is public.
#   Any credential value, or anything that could be used to locate one. This
#   file names paths. Reading it tells you nothing you could authenticate with.
# id
